earlier_scan.note: Retired Glottolog languoid; 'not been able to find evidence that this language exists' (recording was Ormuri); no references at all

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority / Joan L. G. Baart (SIL International). 2012. Request for Change to ISO 639-3 Language Code, Change Request Number 2012-069: Retire [mld] Malakhel (adopted 2013-01-23). 5 pp.
sources.note: Nothing about stress; it is an administrative form. Sec. 3(c), p. 2: 'We have not been able to find evidence that this language exists. As far as we can see, it is not mentioned in the professional linguistic literature. The website of Global Recordings Network contains an audio-recorded story said to be in the Malakhel language; however, I listened to it and identified the language in the audio recording to be Ormuri [oru].' Sec. 3(b): equivalent code element = [oru] Ormuri. Only source cited (p. 4): Kieffer 2003, Grammaire de l'ormuri de Baraki-Barak, which 'does not mention Malakhel'.

Nothing; entry 'has been retired and is featured here only for bookkeeping purposes'; 'Retired in ISO 639-3: No evidence this exists. Change request: 2012-069.. Reason: non-existent. Effective: 2013-01-23'. Zero descriptive references (Glottolog lists no grammar, sketch or phonology).

Would only matter as a second Ormuri stress source for ormu1247, not for this key.
